note: Identity roster for audit-agencysignature-main-tip.ts (fail-CLOSED exemption list).
READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. This file lists the ONLY identities that may be
EXEMPT from carrying an AgencySignature trailer. It is deliberately NOT a list of
agents. The auditor's previous defect was an ALLOWLIST OF AGENTS: a commit whose
Co-authored-by did not match Claude|Codex|Grok|Gemini|Kiro fell through to
'assuming human-authored' and was exempted. That is fail-OPEN -- every persona the
fleet adds is silently exempt until someone audits the auditor. Measured on
origin/main 2026-08-14, it exempted 39 github-actions[bot] commits and 6 commits
trailed with the fleet's own personas (Dejan, Soraya, the shadow, Otto).
The inversion: exemption now requires a POSITIVE match in this file. An identity
nobody listed is agent-or-unknown and MUST sign. A stale roster therefore produces
a FALSE REGRESSION (loud, one-line diff to fix) instead of a FALSE EXEMPTION
(silent, indefinite). That asymmetry is the entire point of the file.
MATCHED ON Co-authored-by ONLY -- never on the git author field. 155 of the last
300 commits on origin/main are authored 'Aaron Stainback <aaron_bond@yahoo.com>'
and committed by 'GitHub <noreply@github.com>': that is GitHub's squash-merge
attribution of AGENT pull requests to the merging human's account. Treating the
author field as a human signal would exempt the majority of main. The one
exception is machineLanes, which may also match author/committer, and only for a
commit that carries no Co-authored-by at all (the direct-push telemetry lanes).
Comparison is on the e-mail address, lowercased (ASCII), exact. Display names are
informational only.
RESIDUAL HOLE, stated rather than papered over: a commit produced by an agent but
pushed through a human's GitHub credential is attributed by GitHub to that human,
and this roster will exempt it. The credential is the human-authorization boundary
in this repo, so that is the intended reading -- but it is an inference from the
credential, not evidence a human wrote the diff. The HUMAN-ROSTER-EXEMPT count is
printed in every audit summary so the size of that inference stays visible.
SECOND SECTION, ADDED 2026-08-15: 'externalActors'. Read by the PRE-MERGE validator
(validate-agencysignature-pr-body.ts) and by NOTHING else -- the post-merge auditor
reads 'humans' and 'machineLanes' only. The two sections are disjoint and keyed
differently on purpose: a commit has e-mails, a proposal has a forge actor identity.
WHY IT IS NOT A SYNTHESISED TRAILER. A trailer is a SELF-attestation: the actor says
who it is, what model it ran, and whether a human reviewed it. Dependabot is a third
party -- it will never emit one, and writing one that claims to come FROM it would be
forging an attestation inside an attestation convention, which is the one thing the
convention exists to make impossible. So the profile below is REPO-ASSERTED: it is
what WE know about a known external actor, recorded here, in git, in text, by whoever
merged the row. The validator PRINTS it and never emits it as a trailer.
See .claude/rules/no-directives.md -- source is not authorization; anyone may attach
a source, the attestation stays the actor's own.
MATCHED ON THE PR AUTHOR (github.event.pull_request.user.login), never on
github.actor. github.actor is whoever TRIGGERED the event -- on an `edited` event
that is the editor, so matching it would let any rostered actor exempt somebody
else's PR by touching it. Exact equality on the trimmed, lowercased login; no
prefixes, no globs, no `endsWith('[bot]')`. An empty or absent author is NOT exempt.

externalActors.name: Dependabot
externalActors.why: GitHub's dependency-update service. THIRD PARTY: we do not run it, cannot change what it writes in a PR body, and cannot make it emit a trailer. Every other unsigned PR-opening lane in this repo is OUR workflow and is fixed by making the workflow sign (pr-archive-on-merge.yml #10764; merge-heartbeats-to-main.ts, this PR). This one cannot be, so it is recorded instead.
externalActors.profileEvidence: Measured 2026-08-15 on PR #10753: pull_request.user.login = 'dependabot[bot]', user.type = 'Bot'. Opens PRs on a schedule with no human in the loop; the diff is a manifest version bump generated from the advisory/registry feed, not a model sample. A human still has to MERGE it -- that is the review, and it happens after this gate, which is why Human-Review is 'none' here and not 'explicit'.
